name: Low Cost Porta Cabin
description:
Low Cost Porta Cabin — Where the Price Comes From and What You Trade

A low cost porta cabin from SAMAN is not a structurally weaker product — it is a specification decision. Understanding which choices reduce the price — and which are never reduced regardless of budget — is the only way to know whether the lowest available price delivers what your deployment actually needs.

What Makes a SAMAN Porta Cabin Low Cost

The saving never comes from the frame. Every SAMAN porta cabin — lowest price to highest — carries the same welded IS 2062 mild-steel structure. On the low cost line the price comes down through the specification built around that frame: 0.8–1.0 mm corrugated MS wall sheet and a 1.2 mm roof sheet instead of the standard line's heavier gauge, 6 mm pre-laminated board lining in place of 8 mm MDF, and an entry-grade finish package — while the cabin still arrives complete: insulated, lined, floored and wired. Across the nine standard sizes this works out to ₹1,104–₹1,320 per sq ft ex-GST, about 4% below our standard porta cabin line.

Every SAMAN low cost porta cabin leaves our Bengaluru and Greater Noida units on the same welded 100×50×3 mm MS C-channel chassis as our standard line — the load-bearing frame does not get cheaper when the price does. Where the saving genuinely comes from is the entry-level specification built on top of that frame: 0.8–1.0 mm corrugated MS wall sheet and a 1.2 mm corrugated sloped roof instead of the standard line's heavier gauge, 6 mm pre-laminated board lining in place of 8 mm MDF, and an 18 mm BWP plywood floor finished with 1.5 mm vinyl. It still arrives as a complete, finished cabin: insulated with 12 mm heatlon or 25 mm glass wool in the walls and 25–50 mm glass wool under the roof, powder-coated aluminium sliding windows with safety grills, a 32 mm waterproof flush door on an MS frame, LED lighting, fan and socket points concealed-wired for 240 V single-phase supply, and one primer plus two enamel coats over the shell. Because all nine standard sizes are built to this one repeatable specification, there is no bespoke premium in the price — you are paying for a dependable, finished, insulated site cabin at the lowest rate in our range, not for a lighter frame or an unfinished box. For guard posts, site offices, stores and staff rooms where budget decides, this is the sensible entry point; when a project needs heavier-gauge cladding, PUF-panel thermal performance or a higher interior grade, the same cabin steps up to our standard and luxury lines. Delivered and installed across South and North India, typically in 7–21 working days, with transport and custom fit-out quoted separately so the base price stays honest.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the IS 2062 structural frame really identical at the lowest price as at the highest price — or is a lower grade used at entry-level? Yes — the IS 2062 Grade A mild-steel structural frame is identical across all SAMAN price tiers. The base frame, corner posts and roof frame use the same IS 2062 steel at entry level as at premium specification. What changes on the low cost line is the shell and finish around that frame: 0.8–1.0 mm wall sheet and 1.2 mm roof sheet (vs the standard line's heavier gauge), 6 mm pre-laminated lining (vs 8 mm MDF), and an entry-grade fit-out. The skeleton is the same at every price point.

Can insulation be added to an entry-level porta cabin after it has been delivered — as a retrofit? Every low cost cabin already ships insulated — 12 mm heatlon or 25 mm glass wool in the walls and 25–50 mm glass wool under the roof. If a site later needs higher thermal performance, additional glass-wool packing can be done in the field by a local fabricator, but a PUF sandwich-panel upgrade is not practical as a retrofit — it requires full panel replacement. If PUF-level insulation may be needed, specifying it at the original order stage (our standard or luxury lines) is significantly more economical than upgrading later.

What is the minimum price for a 10×10 ft porta cabin from SAMAN and exactly what does it include? A SAMAN 10×10 ft low cost porta cabin is ₹1,32,000 ex-GST (₹1,55,760 including 18% GST, HSN 9406). That is a complete, finished cabin: welded IS 2062 MS frame, 0.8–1.0 mm corrugated steel shell with 1.2 mm roof, insulated walls and roof, 6 mm pre-laminated lined interior, 18 mm BWP plywood floor with 1.5 mm vinyl finish, a 32 mm waterproof flush door on an MS frame, powder-coated aluminium sliding windows with mosquito mesh, LED lighting, fan and socket points with a mini DB — concealed-wired for 240 V single-phase supply. Transport, installation and any custom fit-out are quoted separately.

What is the price of a low cost porta cabin per square foot? A SAMAN low cost porta cabin works out to roughly ₹1,104–₹1,320 per sq ft ex-GST depending on size — larger cabins cost less per sq ft. The prices in the size table are complete, finished-cabin prices, not per-sq-ft estimates, and they sit about 4% below our standard porta cabin line.

Does "low cost" mean lower quality or a weaker cabin? No. The welded structural MS frame (100×50×3 mm IS 2062 C-channel chassis) is identical across our low cost, standard and luxury lines, and every low cost cabin ships finished — lined interior, vinyl floor, insulation, windows and full electricals. The saving comes from lighter wall/roof sheet gauge (0.8–1.0 mm walls, 1.2 mm roof) and economical finish grades, plus fixed standard sizes — never from cutting the structure.

What is included in the base low cost price, and what is quoted separately? The base price covers the complete factory-built cabin — frame, corrugated steel shell and roof, laminate interior, vinyl flooring, standard insulation, sliding windows with grills, MS door, LED lighting, fan and socket points. Transport, installation, GST (18%, HSN 9406) and any custom fit-out, furniture or attached toilet are quoted separately so the cabin price stays transparent.

What is the difference between the low cost porta cabin and the standard porta cabin? Same nine sizes and the same welded MS chassis; the low cost line uses 0.8–1.0 mm wall sheet and a 1.2 mm roof (vs 1.2/1.4 mm on the standard line), 6 mm board lining (vs 8 mm MDF), a 32 mm flush door and 3 mm window glass — a genuine entry-level specification at a lower price. The standard line adds heavier gauge and finish; for PUF panels and premium interiors, see our luxury porta cabin.

Can I upgrade insulation or finish later? Yes — insulation and interior finishes can be specified up front or planned as a later retrofit; tell us the use and climate at enquiry and we will advise whether the entry specification is adequate or a heavier-gauge / PUF-panel step-up is worth it for your site.

Do you deliver low cost porta cabins outside Bangalore? Yes — we deliver and install across South and North India from our Bengaluru and Greater Noida units, typically in 7–21 working days. Free delivery covers Bengaluru city and the Delhi-NCR belt (Ghaziabad, Gurugram, Faridabad, Noida, Greater Noida); elsewhere transport is quoted by distance.

Are custom sizes available on the low cost line? The nine standard sizes carry the lowest pricing because they are built to one repeatable specification. Custom sizes are possible but are quoted separately and will not carry the standard-size economy rate.
